p5PauseAdjudication.doesThatMakeItSystematic: NOT on this evidence, and the transport review just measured the general question. Within this window alone: the two failures are on two DIFFERENT hosts and two DIFFERENT registrable domains belonging to two different organisations; 40 of the window's 42 observations resolved cleanly to PUBLIC IPv4 addresses across 5 distinct hosts within three minutes of them; the vantage was re-proved compliant immediately before each item, with ipv4only.arpa returning A records and no AAAA each time; and across the whole generation all 9 DNS_NAME_NOT_FOUND rows sit on 9 DISTINCT registrable domains over 4 calendar days. A resolver that answered 40 queries correctly and returned an authoritative negative for two unrelated names is behaving as a resolver, not failing
p5PauseAdjudication.whatIsNewAndWorthTheOwnersAttention: this is the THIRD consecutive window to end on P5, and the first in which BOTH low-yield items carried the same failure subtype. The bound transport review, taken minutes earlier, found no common systemic cause and this window's own evidence does not overturn it - but the repetition is now a pattern in the SAMPLE, and whether the acquisition capability should be extended to targets whose published website hostname does not resolve is a CAPABILITY question the owner has not been asked
p5PauseAdjudication.whatThisAdjudicationDoesNotDo: it proposes no repair, no retry, no fallback hostname, no alternate root and no methodology change. A published hostname that does not resolve is the register's value, and substituting another would be guessing
